## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/process
How a Flake Floor Gets Built | Final Finish Edmonton

The sequence How a flake floor actually goes. Six steps, in this order, for a flake floor. Installation usually runs two days, and it varies with the concrete underneath. From this job Final Finish · Edmonton 01 A free estimate Send photos of the floor, or book a visit. Either works, and both are free. Denis wants to see the concrete, what is on it now, and any cracks you already know about. 02 Grinding The slab is ground to open the surface so the coating can bond. It is loud, dusty work, and the room has to be empty before it starts. The diamond grinding guide explains the profile it leaves. 03 Cosmetic crack filling Visible cracks are filled so they do not read through the finish. If something turns up that is structural rather than cosmetic, you hear about it then, not later. The cracks and spalling guide covers what gets assessed. 04 The flake broadcast Flake is broadcast into the coat while it is still open. This is where the colour and the pattern of the floor are set. The featured colours are on the finishes page. 05 The scrape Once it has set, the surface is scraped back. That is what turns a loose broadcast into a flat floor you can walk on and clean. 06 The top coat The last coat goes over everything. Where a room needs more grip, an Anti-Slip Coating goes on instead, and that is a decision we make with you. The slip-resistance guide covers the trade-offs. Two things this page will not tell you: when you can park on it, and what it costs.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/auto-shop-floor-coating/
Auto Shop Floor Coating Planning | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / commercial commercial · Edmonton floor library Auto Shop Floor Coating Planning Planning an auto shop or detailing bay floor coating in Edmonton: fluids, hot tires, lifts, washdown and grip, bright floors, and keeping the bays working. Updated September 22, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor What an auto shop floor has to survive A service bay floor takes more than almost any other: motor oil, brake fluid, coolant, battery acid, solvents, degreasers, hot tires, jack stands, lift posts, creepers, and dropped tools, every day. A coating turns bare, stained concrete into a surface that sheds fluids, cleans quickly, and reflects light. Getting there means choosing the system for those exposures and planning the work around the bays. Final Finish’s commercial work covers surface preparation, crack filling, and anti-slip finishes. Fluids and chemical resistance Every coating resists some chemicals better than others. Brake fluid and some solvents are harder on coatings than water-based fluids. The product documents include chemical resistance information, often as a table of substances and exposure times. Ask for it, check it against what your shop actually uses, and plan for prompt cleanup. A spill wiped up in minutes is a different exposure from a puddle left over a weekend. Keep safety data sheets for the coating products as well as the shop’s own chemicals.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/barn-farm-shop-floor-coating/
Barn and Farm Shop Floor Coating | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / planning planning · Edmonton floor library Barn and Farm Shop Floor Coating Planning a barn or farm shop floor coating in Alberta: heavy equipment, fuel and oil, washdown and grip, cold shops, and the logistics of a very large floor. Updated September 22, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor What makes a farm shop floor different A farm shop is a garage, a workshop, and sometimes a wash bay in one building, at a bigger scale. The floor takes tractor tires, dropped parts, fuel, hydraulic oil, and washdown water, often in a building that is heated only some of the time. A coating can handle that, but the system and the preparation have to be chosen for it. Barns, workshops, and shops are among the spaces Final Finish coats. Heavy equipment and point loads Tractors, loaders, and trailers bring weight and grit. Plan for: Hot tires. Tires coming in off hot pavement can soften some top coats and lift marks. The hot-tire pickup guide explains why the top coat choice matters. Point loads. Jack stands, lift pads, and implement stands concentrate weight. Ask how the system handles them, and put plates under stands. Dropped steel. Chips happen where heavy parts fall. A textured flake floor hides small impacts better than a thin, glossy solid colour, and small chips can be repaired. Tracks and chains. Anything steel-tracked, chained, or dragged will damage a coating. Keep it off the coated area or plan a separate zone.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/basement-concrete-floor-coating/
Basement Floor Coating Basics | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / planning planning · Edmonton floor library Basement Floor Coating Basics Plan an Edmonton basement flake floor around moisture, ventilation, slab condition, and how the room will be used before daily life starts again in the house. Updated September 18, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor A basement coating should be the last decision in a short chain, not the first. Begin by deciding whether the room has a water problem, a concrete problem, or simply an unfinished surface. A coating can change colour, cleanability, texture, and light reflection. It cannot redirect groundwater, repair a failed drain, or make an unsound slab sound. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. 1. Rule out active water entry Inspect after snowmelt or heavy rain if possible. Record where dampness appears: at a wall-floor joint, around a penetration, beneath stored objects, or across the open slab. Photograph mineral deposits, dark areas, peeling paint, and previous patches. Note sump operation, plumbing leaks, downspout issues, and whether exterior drainage work is underway. This distinction matters because a moisture reading does not identify the source of liquid water. ASTM F2170 measures relative humidity inside a concrete slab at the time of testing; ASTM explicitly notes that results describe the slab’s moisture condition only when the test is performed ( ASTM F2170-19a ).

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/cold-weather-floor-coating-edmonton/
Cold-Weather Floor Coating Tips | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / local guide local guide · Edmonton floor library Cold-Weather Floor Coating Tips Plan Edmonton cold-weather floor coating around garage temperatures, cure windows, and diamond-grind prep so winter installs stay controlled and documented. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor An Edmonton winter does not automatically rule out a floor-coating project. It changes what must be controlled and recorded. The important conditions are not the temperature in a weather app alone; they are the temperature and moisture conditions at the slab, in the work zone, and in the stored materials throughout preparation, application, and cure. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. Environment and Climate Change Canada’s Edmonton city dataset includes daily temperature normals, extremes, and counts of cold days for the 1991–2020 normal period ( Edmonton climate normals ). That official record supports a practical conclusion: a winter quote needs a cold-weather control plan, not an assumption that an attached garage or loading area will remain suitable. Think in zones, not one thermostat reading Divide the project into four temperature zones: Outside: affects open-door events, deliveries, exhaust placement, and replacement air. Material storage: affects the temperature of resin, hardener, repair products, and aggregates before mixing. Room air: affects worker comfort, ventilation, and product cure.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/commercial-flooring-downtime-planning/
Commercial Floor Downtime Plan | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / commercial commercial · Edmonton floor library Commercial Floor Downtime Plan Build a commercial floor coating downtime plan for Edmonton spaces covering phased access, cure timing, diamond-grind dust control, and return-to-service steps. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor “How many days will we be closed?” is the wrong first scheduling question. Start with the business events that cannot overlap the work: customers crossing the area, forklifts serving a dock, sanitation cycles, emergency egress, deliveries, food preparation, patient movement, or access to electrical and mechanical rooms. Then build the coating sequence between those constraints. For local scope options, see our commercial epoxy flooring. The result is a shutdown plan with decision gates, not a promise based on a calendar alone. Create an operations map before requesting dates Walk the area with the facility lead, installer, health-and-safety contact, and the person who can authorize reopening. Mark: pedestrian, cart, pallet-jack, and vehicle routes; exits, fire equipment, panels, drains, coolers, and shutoffs; production equipment that stays, moves, or needs disconnection; adjacent occupants and shared ventilation; receiving hours, cleaning shifts, and contractor access; temperature-sensitive inventory; noise-, dust-, or odour-sensitive operations; the smallest zones that can function independently.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/concrete-cracks-spalling-floor-coating/
Cracks and Spalling Before Coat | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library Cracks and Spalling Before Coat Assess concrete cracks and spalling before an Edmonton floor coating so repairs, diamond grinding, and flake or solid finishes sit on a sound documented slab. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Cracks and spalls are not one defect. A narrow dormant crack, a moving joint, a thin scaled surface, and a deep patch around corroding reinforcement need different responses. Covering every line with the same filler may improve a photograph while leaving the cause and movement unchanged. For local scope options, see our Surface Preparation. ACI’s concrete-repair guide organizes repair work around evaluation, selection of repair strategy and materials, preparation, application, and quality control ( ACI PRC-546-23 ). Use that sequence before deciding what the finished floor should look like. Name the condition accurately Crack: a separation in the concrete. Record width, length, location, moisture, edge level, and whether it changes. Control or contraction joint: an intentional plane intended to manage where shrinkage cracking occurs. It is a floor detail, not automatically a defect. Construction joint: where separate concrete placements meet. Its movement and loading conditions may differ from a random crack. Scaling: loss of a thin surface layer, often seen as flaking or a rough shallow area. Spall: a localized loss of concrete with measurable depth.

---

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/concrete-moisture-testing-floor-coatings/
Concrete Moisture Testing Guide | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library Concrete Moisture Testing Guide Use concrete moisture testing before Edmonton floor coatings to match methods, locations, and limits to the slab rather than one casual meter reading. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor A concrete moisture test is useful only when three things are named: the method, the installation conditions, and the coating system’s acceptance limit. A meter swept across the surface may help an assessor compare locations, but it does not become an ASTM test merely because it displays a number. For local scope options, see our Surface Preparation. Moisture testing also does not answer every water question. It does not locate a plumbing leak, prove exterior drainage is sound, or guarantee how a slab will behave forever.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/concrete-polishing-vs-floor-coating/
Concrete Polish vs Floor Coat | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / local guide local guide · Edmonton floor library Concrete Polish vs Floor Coat Compare concrete polishing and floor coating for Edmonton slabs by use, maintenance, and appearance so garage or commercial goals drive the system choice. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor The first question is not “Which lasts longer?” It is “Do you want the concrete itself to be the finished surface, or do you want a separate material system over it?” Polishing refines and exposes the slab. A resinous coating builds a film or system above the slab. That basic choice shapes appearance, repairs, moisture tolerance, maintenance, and future changes. For local scope options, see our Surface Preparation.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/concrete-repair-mortars-floor-coatings/
Repair Mortars Before Coating | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library Repair Mortars Before Coating Understand concrete repair mortars before Edmonton floor coatings: compatible patches, diamond-grind prep, and recoat timing that fit the selected epoxy system. Updated September 18, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor A repair mortar replaces missing or removed concrete so the floor again has the shape, support, and surface needed for its next use. It is not automatically a crack filler, moisture barrier, levelling compound, or structural design solution. The correct role depends on the defect and on what will be installed above it. For local scope options, see our Surface Preparation. ACI’s repair guide treats condition evaluation, repair strategy, material selection, surface preparation, application, and quality control as one process ( ACI PRC-546-23 ). Skipping directly to a bag or cartridge reverses that sequence.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/concrete-sealer-vs-floor-coating/
Concrete Sealer vs Floor Coating | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / materials materials · Edmonton floor library Concrete Sealer vs Floor Coating Concrete sealer or floor coating? How penetrating sealers, film sealers, and epoxy coatings differ on salt, stains, wear, looks, and recoating in Edmonton. Updated September 22, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor The short answer A sealer protects concrete from water and salt getting in. A coating puts a new wearing surface on top. Sealers are thin, mostly invisible, and need reapplying. A coating system, like an epoxy flake floor, is a built-up layer that changes how the floor looks, cleans, and wears. Which one makes sense depends on what the floor faces and how you want it to look. Three things people call sealer Penetrating sealers soak into the concrete and line its pores. Silanes and siloxanes are the common ones. They repel water and salt brine and leave the surface looking much the same. They are widely used on outdoor concrete such as driveways and walks. Densifiers react with the concrete to harden the surface and cut down on dusting. They are used on bare interior floors and under polished concrete. Film-forming sealers, often acrylic, sit on top as a thin clear layer with some sheen. They wear off under traffic and tires and need reapplying. The ACI guide to protective treatments for concrete covers these families, and more, and how to choose among them for a given exposure.

---

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/concrete-surface-profile-csp/
Concrete Surface Profile (CSP) | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library Concrete Surface Profile (CSP) Learn concrete surface profile (CSP) in plain language so Edmonton floor coatings get the diamond-grind or blast texture the manufacturer actually specifies. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Concrete surface profile, usually shortened to CSP, describes the roughness and texture left after concrete preparation. Imagine the difference between a smooth countertop, coarse sandpaper, and exposed stone: each presents a different shape for the next material to contact. CSP gives project teams a shared visual reference for that shape. For local scope options, see our Surface Preparation. It does not certify that the concrete is clean, dry, strong, or ready to coat. Those are separate acceptance questions. What the CSP numbers mean ICRI Guideline 310.2R includes benchmark profiles and discusses the capabilities, operating requirements, and limitations of preparation methods used before sealers, coatings, overlays, and repairs ( ICRI 310.2R ). The ICRI system runs from CSP 1 through CSP 10, with the visual texture becoming progressively more aggressive. The number is a comparator, not a recipe. “Diamond grind” and “shot blast” are methods; “CSP 2” or “CSP 4” is an intended surface result. Tool type, media, speed, pressure, concrete hardness, existing finish, operator technique, and repeated passes can change what a method produces.

---

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/diamond-grinding-concrete-preparation/
Diamond Grinding for Floor Prep | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library Diamond Grinding for Floor Prep See how diamond grinding prepares Edmonton concrete for garage flake or commercial coatings, including dust control, edges, and profile checks before coating. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Diamond grinding uses rotating abrasive segments to remove a controlled layer from concrete. In floor-coating work, its value is not that it makes concrete look scratched. It can remove certain coatings and surface contaminants, open the surface, flatten small projections, and expose defects that were hidden. The required result is a sound, clean, suitably profiled substrate, not a specified number of machine passes. For local scope options, see our Surface Preparation. What grinding can realistically do Depending on the tooling and concrete, grinding may: remove paint, thin coatings, adhesive residue, laitance, or surface sealer; reduce ridges, trowel marks, and minor high spots; prepare edges and small rooms that larger equipment cannot access; blend patch boundaries; reveal cracks, weak areas, oil penetration, and previous repairs; produce a profile appropriate for some coating or repair materials. ICRI 310.2R summarizes concrete preparation methods by capabilities, operating needs, limitations, and benchmark surface profiles ( ICRI 310.2R ). That source is useful precisely because method selection is not one-size-fits-all.

---

DIY vs Pro Floor Coating Guide | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / planning planning · Edmonton floor library DIY vs Pro Floor Coating Guide Weigh DIY versus professional floor coating for Edmonton garages using prep, diamond grinding, flake systems, cure control, and long-term maintenance factors. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor A DIY floor coating is not simply the professional version without labour cost. The homeowner becomes the assessor, specifier, equipment operator, material handler, installer, quality-control lead, and repair crew. That can be reasonable on a small, sound, accessible slab with a forgiving finish. It becomes risky as substrate uncertainty, preparation hazards, timing pressure, or appearance expectations rise. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. Use this framework before buying material. Score seven project dimensions Give each category 0, 1, or 2 points.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/epoxy-floor-odours-ventilation/
Plan Epoxy Odours and Ventilation | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / planning planning · Edmonton floor library Plan Epoxy Odours and Ventilation Plan epoxy floor odours and ventilation for Edmonton homes and shops with source control, access routes, and occupancy timing without inventing product claims. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Odour is useful as a complaint (someone is experiencing something in a place), but it is a poor instrument. A strong smell does not quantify exposure, and little or no smell does not prove that a product or work area is safe. Plan an epoxy floor project from the exact products, their safety data, the building’s air pathways, and the people who use the space. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. Start with a product inventory, not the word “epoxy” A floor system can include degreaser, crack filler, repair mortar, primer, resin, hardener, colour coat, broadcast aggregate, topcoat, and cleaning solvent. Each may have different hazards and handling controls. Obtain the current Canadian SDS and product data sheet for every component before scheduling. CCOHS explains that SDS sections cover hazard identification, composition, first aid, firefighting, accidental release, handling and storage, exposure controls and personal protection, physical properties, stability, and disposal, among other information ( CCOHS SDS guide ). Review the complete documents; a VOC figure or “low odour” description is not a replacement.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/epoxy-flooring-vs-concrete-paint/
Epoxy Flooring vs Concrete Paint | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / planning planning · Edmonton floor library Epoxy Flooring vs Concrete Paint Compare epoxy flooring and concrete paint for Edmonton garages: film build, diamond-grind prep, flake options, and durability that paint alone rarely matches. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Concrete paint and epoxy flooring can both add colour to a slab, but the useful comparison is not “paint versus epoxy” as two uniform products. Concrete paints vary by binder and intended use. Epoxy products range from thin water-based coatings to primers, high-build body coats, mortars, and multi-layer broadcast systems. Compare named products and complete scopes. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. The fastest way to separate them Ask for the product data sheet and answer four questions: Is it one component or does it cure after measured components are mixed? What prepared concrete condition and profile does it require? What dry-film thickness or application rate is specified? Is it a standalone finish or one layer in a tested system? A label using “epoxy” as an adjective does not answer those questions. Sika’s official epoxy-coating catalogue, for example, includes binders, primers/sealers, membranes, pigmented finishes, and high-build products rather than one generic epoxy ( Sika epoxy coating catalogue ). This is a bounded illustration of category breadth, not a product recommendation.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/flake-vs-metallic-vs-solid-epoxy/
Flake vs Metallic vs Solid Floors | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / materials materials · Edmonton floor library Flake vs Metallic vs Solid Floors How flake, metallic, and solid colour floors differ in look, wear, and daily use. Final Finish installs flake floors. This comparison stays educational. Updated September 22, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor This page compares flake, metallic, and solid colour floors so the differences are clear. The floors Final Finish installs are flake. We use Torginol products. The quick comparison Flake is the practical choice for most garages. A base coat, a broadcast of coloured flake, a scrape, and a clear top coat make a textured, speckled floor that hides dust, grit, and small scratches. Solid colour is one even colour under a top coat. It looks clean and architectural and brightens a room, but it shows dust, tire marks, and scratches sooner. Metallic is poured and worked by hand so metallic pigments settle into swirls and depth. No two floors are alike. It is the most decorative of the three and the least forgiving of dust and wear. All three are epoxy systems on prepared concrete. The preparation underneath follows the same idea for each, because the prepared surface has to suit the coating, as the ICRI guideline on surface preparation sets out. What changes is what you see, and how the floor lives with daily use. How each one looks Flake reads as texture from across the room and as colour up close. The colour comes from the blend, a mix of tones and chip sizes.

---

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/floor-coating-contractor-checklist/
Floor Coating Contractor Checks | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / planning planning · Edmonton floor library Floor Coating Contractor Checks Use this Edmonton floor coating contractor checklist to compare prep, diamond grinding, flake or solid finishes, schedules, and documentation before you hire. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Use this checklist to make bids comparable. It does not tell you which contractor to hire; it reveals whether each contractor has priced the same floor, preparation, system, safety obligations, and hand-off. For local scope options, see our commercial epoxy flooring. Before inviting bids Write the room use, traffic, chemicals, cleaning method, wet conditions, texture priorities, and appearance expectations. Mark cracks, joints, spalls, drains, slopes, edges, old coatings, oil, damp areas, and fixed equipment on a floor plan. State access hours, available power, water, heating, ventilation control, storage, and waste restrictions. Identify the owner representative who can approve hidden-condition changes. Give every bidder the same photos, floor plan, service conditions, and required bid format. Do not begin with a desired resin name alone. A product can only be evaluated against the substrate and use. Contractor and project administration Legal business name and contact information appear on the proposal. The proposal identifies who supervises the work and who performs specialized testing.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/floor-coating-recoat-windows/
Why Floor Recoat Timing Matters | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / materials materials · Edmonton floor library Why Floor Recoat Timing Matters Learn why floor coating recoat windows matter in Edmonton installs, from intercoat adhesion to garage temperature swings that change manufacturer timing. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor A recoat window is the period in which one layer may receive the next layer under the manufacturer’s stated conditions and preparation. It has two edges: too early and too late. “Apply tomorrow” is not a recoat specification because temperature, product, layer thickness, humidity, and the condition of the first coat can change the permitted timing. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. Minimum and maximum solve different problems The minimum wait helps ensure the first layer has progressed far enough to accept the next operation without unacceptable disturbance, solvent entrapment, marking, or other product-specific problems. The maximum wait marks the point beyond which the manufacturer may require additional cleaning, abrasion, primer, or another procedure to establish intercoat bond. The exact reason and remedy depend on the chemistry and system. Do not confuse these times: pot life: usable time after components are mixed; working time: practical application period; tack-free or dry-to-touch time; recoat window; foot-traffic time; vehicle or equipment traffic time; full cure or chemical-service time.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/floor-coating-terminology-glossary/
Floor Coating Terminology Guide | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / glossary glossary · Edmonton floor library Floor Coating Terminology Guide Decode floor coating terminology like profile, diamond grind, flake broadcast, primer, topcoat, and cure so Edmonton buyers can read proposals without fog. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Flooring terms often collapse a detailed requirement into one word. Use this glossary to expand the shorthand, then ask which product, test method, condition, or acceptance value applies to your project. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. Substrate and preparation Abrasion: Mechanical wearing of a surface. In preparation, abrasion may remove a layer and create texture; the scope should name the method and required result. Bond-inhibiting contaminant: Material such as oil, dust, curing compound, adhesive, wax, or incompatible sealer that can interfere with adhesion. Identification and removal must be method-specific. Concrete surface profile (CSP): ICRI’s visual and tactile scale for comparing prepared-concrete roughness. ICRI 310.2R provides benchmark profiles and describes preparation methods and limitations ( ICRI 310.2R ). CSP does not by itself prove cleanliness, soundness, or moisture suitability. Diamond grinding: Preparation using rotating diamond tooling. It may remove coatings, laitance, or high spots and leave a particular profile, depending on tools, concrete, and technique. Laitance: A weak, fine surface layer on concrete.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/floor-coating-voc-basics/
VOC Basics for Floor Coatings | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / materials materials · Edmonton floor library VOC Basics for Floor Coatings Get VOC basics for Edmonton floor coating decisions: what labels mean, how ventilation fits garage and commercial installs, and which proposal questions to ask. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor VOC means volatile organic compound. In a floor-coating decision, a VOC number can help compare a defined environmental property of products when the calculation basis and category match. It cannot by itself tell you whether the coating is odourless, non-toxic, safe for immediate occupancy, durable, or appropriate for a particular slab. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. What “volatile” describes Health Canada describes VOCs as a large group of chemicals present in indoor and outdoor air and identifies products such as paints and solvents among indoor sources ( Health Canada VOC guidance ). “Volatile” concerns a substance’s tendency to enter the air; it is not a complete hazard ranking. Different VOCs have different health effects, odour thresholds, and exposure limits. A floor system may also contain important non-VOC hazards, including ingredients that affect skin or eyes. That is why VOC content, hazard communication, ventilation, and floor performance remain separate review tracks.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/heated-garage-floor-coating/
Coating a Heated Garage Floor | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / local guide local guide · Edmonton floor library Coating a Heated Garage Floor Coating a garage floor with in-floor heat in Edmonton: where the tubing runs, slab temperature during the install, moisture, and what to ask before the quote. Updated September 22, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Can you coat a heated garage floor? Yes. Garages with in-floor heat are common around Edmonton, and a coating works well on them. A heated slab changes three things about the job: how deep anything can safely cut into the concrete, how warm the slab is while the coating goes down, and how moisture moves through it. None of them is a reason not to coat. All three are reasons to mention the heat before anyone writes a quote. Where the tubing is, and why it matters Hydronic in-floor heat runs warm water through plastic tubing cast into the slab. The tubing sits well below the surface, and surface preparation removes only a thin layer, so normal diamond grinding does not reach it. The risk comes from deeper work: cutting out a crack, removing a broken section, drilling for anchors or posts, or cutting a new joint. Before any of that, the tubing has to be located. If you have the layout drawings from construction, share them. If not, running the heat and scanning the floor with a thermal camera shows the tubing as warm lines. Mark them before any deep repair starts. Heated slabs crack and curl for the same reasons other slabs do.

Updated September 14, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Map the workout before choosing the finish A home gym is rarely one uniform exposure. A treadmill applies repeating vibration in one spot, a power rack concentrates loads at its feet, a stretching area sees bare skin and frequent wiping, and a free-weight zone may see impact. Draw the room and mark equipment, travel paths, dropped-weight areas, water bottles, exterior doors, floor drains, and storage. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. This map quickly reveals an important distinction: a coating can provide a cleanable finish over suitable concrete, but it is not cushioning. Where weights may be dropped, use a protection strategy designed for the equipment and exercise rather than expecting the coating to absorb impact. Decide where mats belong Rubber tiles, lifting platforms, and equipment mats can protect selected zones and add comfort, but they introduce interfaces. Ask the mat or equipment manufacturer about backing compatibility, staining or plasticizer transfer, ventilation, and load distribution. Ask the coating manufacturer whether the proposed mat can be placed on the cured finish and whether periodic lifting is recommended.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/how-epoxy-floor-coatings-cure/
Epoxy Floor Coating Cure Basics | Final Finish Epoxy

Updated September 18, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Cure is chemistry, not simply drying Two-part epoxy coatings develop through a chemical reaction after resin and hardener are combined. That makes cure different from a water puddle evaporating. The mix ratio, mixing method, material temperature, slab temperature, room conditions, film build, and elapsed time can all affect the process described by the product manufacturer. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. Use only the terms and conditions in the current technical data sheet for every layer in the actual system. The working clock starts at mixing Once components are mixed, the applicator has a limited working period defined by the product document. Material held in a container may behave differently from material spread across a floor because the mass and heat flow differ. This is why a crew plans batch size, labour, tools, edges, and transitions before mixing.

Updated September 14, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor “Hybrid” describes a combination, not a specification A hybrid floor system uses more than one material family or product type to perform different jobs. Kitchens and bathrooms are among the spaces Final Finish coats. The questions are about what is under the current floor, how the room handles water, and how the work fits around a household. ## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/levelling-concrete-before-coating/
Levelling a Floor Before Coating | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library Levelling a Floor Before Coating Levelling concrete before a floor coating in Edmonton: flat versus level, grinding high spots, filling low spots, underlayments, and why garage floors slope. Updated September 22, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Why levelling comes before coating A floor coating is thin. It follows the concrete under it, so a dip, a lip, or a ridge in the slab shows through the finished floor. Levelling deals with those first: grinding down what is high, filling what is low, and smoothing the transitions. Final Finish does concrete levelling and restoration as part of its concrete work, alongside repair and diamond grinding. Flat is not the same as level Two words, two different things: Flat means the surface has no bumps or dips over a short distance. A flat floor can still slope. Level means the floor is horizontal overall. Garages are usually not meant to be level. They slope toward the overhead door or a floor drain so meltwater runs out instead of pooling. Levelling a garage does not mean taking that slope away. It means taking out the low spots where water sits, the lips at cracks, and the ridges at old patches, so the floor drains the way it was built to. Large commercial floors put numbers on this. ASTM E1155 defines the FF and FL numbers used to measure flatness and levelness. Most homes do not need that precision, but the idea is the same: measure, then correct.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/new-concrete-before-floor-coating/
New Concrete Before Floor Coating | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library New Concrete Before Floor Coating Coating a new garage floor in Edmonton: why new concrete needs time, curing versus drying, curing compounds, laitance, moisture tests, and builder questions. Updated September 22, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor How long should new concrete wait before it is coated? Long enough to cure, and to dry to the coating’s limit. New concrete gains strength over weeks, and it holds a lot of water while it does. Coating manufacturers set a minimum age and a moisture limit for their products, and a moisture test confirms the slab has reached it. On a new-build garage, that often means the coating goes down well after move-in. It is worth the wait. A coating applied over a slab that is still wet can trap that moisture, then blister or lose its bond. Curing and drying are not the same thing Curing is the chemical reaction that hardens concrete. It needs water and time, and it carries on for weeks after the pour. The ACI guide to curing covers how curing is done and why it matters for strength and surface quality. Drying is the slab giving up the extra water that was needed to place and finish it. A slab can be well cured and still too wet for a coating. That is why a moisture test is the real gate, not the calendar. ASTM F2170 describes measuring relative humidity inside the slab, and the product documents say what reading is acceptable.

---

Plan an Office Floor Coating Job | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / commercial commercial · Edmonton floor library Plan an Office Floor Coating Job Plan an Edmonton office floor coating around occupancy, noise, diamond-grind dust control, odour management, and phased access so operations stay workable. Then identify what flooring work changes: noise during preparation, dust risk, odour or vapour controls, furniture relocation, blocked paths, power needs, and cure protection. A promise of “low disruption” has no meaning until these constraints are written. Assign decisions before the work Name one facility contact and one contractor contact for every shift. ## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/polyaspartic-flooring-neutral-guide/
Polyaspartic Floors Neutral Guide | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / materials materials · Edmonton floor library Polyaspartic Floors Neutral Guide Read a neutral polyaspartic flooring guide for Edmonton buyers: chemistry, prep, and use questions without claiming Final Finish installs polyaspartic systems. Updated September 14, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor The chemistry name is only the first line Polyaspartic products are often discussed as if the category were a complete floor specification. It is not. A buyer still needs the exact product, substrate assessment, preparation, repair plan, layer sequence, application conditions, decorative finish, maintenance instructions, and return-to-use stages. For local scope options, see our epoxy flooring services. Use neutral language when comparing options. Claims such as “better than epoxy,” “one-day,” or “UV proof” compress many variables into a slogan. Ask which current technical document supports the claim for the named product and the proposed use. Read the proposal from concrete upward Have the contractor list every layer: repairs, primer if used, base or body coat, flake or aggregate, and topcoat. Polyaspartic material may be used in one or several positions; do not assume the same chemistry throughout. For each layer, record manufacturer, product, intended function, application amount or thickness, recoat requirements, and compatibility with the layers around it. If manufacturers are mixed, ask who accepted that interface in writing.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/polyurea-flooring-neutral-guide/
Polyurea Flooring: Neutral Guide | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / materials materials · Edmonton floor library Polyurea Flooring: Neutral Guide Use this neutral polyurea flooring guide to ask better Edmonton buyer questions on chemistry, prep, and suitability without inventing local install claims. Updated September 14, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Polyurea is a family, not one performance profile The word “polyurea” can appear in descriptions of products with different formulations, application methods, and roles. A product may be one layer within a larger system. Buyers should therefore compare exact technical documents and the installed stack, not make decisions from the chemistry name alone. For local scope options, see our epoxy flooring services. Start by asking: where in the floor is the polyurea product used, and what job is it meant to perform? Request a layer-by-layer answer The proposal should identify repair materials, primer, body coat, decorative media, intermediate coats, and topcoat. Beside every layer, list exact product, manufacturer, required preparation, mixing or equipment, application conditions, stated film build, recoat requirements, and return-to-use restrictions. Ask whether the assembly is a published manufacturer system. If it combines sources, request written compatibility support. A layer that bonds well to prepared concrete still has to accept the next layer, and a topcoat has to bond to the decorative or body layer beneath it.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/primer-in-floor-coating-system/
Primer in a Floor Coating System | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / materials materials · Edmonton floor library Primer in a Floor Coating System Learn what a primer does in an Edmonton floor coating system for adhesion, sealing, and sequence before a flake broadcast over ground concrete slabs. Ask Denis. Updated September 14, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Primer is a role, not an automatic extra A primer is the first liquid layer in some floor-coating systems. Depending on the exact product and specification, it may be intended to wet a prepared surface, support adhesion, reduce outgassing risk, create a uniform base, or address a defined moisture condition. Other published systems may not call for a separate primer. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. The useful question is not “Does primer always make a floor better?” It is “Why does this system require this primer on this slab?” Begin with the manufacturer’s system Request the current technical data sheets for primer and next layer. Confirm that they form a documented system and record required surface preparation, mixing, environmental limits, application amount or thickness, recoat conditions, and broadcast instructions if aggregate is used. If products come from different manufacturers, ask who accepted their compatibility in writing. A successful bond between primer and concrete is only half the interface; the next coat must also bond to the primer.

## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/remove-oil-stains-before-floor-coating/
Oil Stains Before Floor Coating | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library Oil Stains Before Floor Coating Handle oil stains before Edmonton garage floor coating with cleaning, verification, and diamond-grind prep so epoxy flake systems are not coating over oil. Updated September 18, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Oil on a garage floor is more than a dark mark. It can be contamination at the surface, liquid held in pores, or evidence of an active vehicle or equipment leak. A coating decision should begin by finding out which condition you have. Covering the stain before resolving that question can hide useful evidence and makes it harder to write a defensible preparation scope. For local scope options, see our residential epoxy flooring. Otherwise, freshly prepared concrete can be contaminated again while the project is being planned. Move leaking equipment to a tray, address the vehicle problem, and keep oily rags or absorbent materials off the slab.

Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor The choice between repairing and replacing a coated floor is rarely determined by the size of the ugly spot alone. A small blister can point to a broader moisture or adhesion issue; a large worn path may be serviceable if the coating remains bonded and the wear mechanism is understood. The useful question is: what failed, why did it fail, and where does sound material begin? For local scope options, see our Surface Preparation. ## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/scratch-maintenance-coated-floor/
Scratch Care for Coated Floors | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / maintenance maintenance · Edmonton floor library Scratch Care for Coated Floors Maintain scratches on coated Edmonton floors with grit control, soft pads, garage flake topcoat habits, and knowing when touch-up needs a professional look. Updated September 18, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor A mark on a coated floor is not automatically a scratch, and every scratch does not need a repair coating. The safest first move is to slow down, identify the type of damage, and consult the maintenance instructions for the installed system. Aggressive trial-and-error cleaning can turn a removable transfer mark into a permanent dull patch. For local scope options, see our commercial epoxy flooring. Sort the mark before choosing a response Look across the floor under low-angle and overhead light. A dark line that sits on the surface may be rubber, plastic, or metal transfer. ## https://www.finalfinishepoxy.ca/resources/shot-blasting-concrete-preparation/
Shot Blasting for Concrete Prep | Final Finish Epoxy

Home / Resources / preparation preparation · Edmonton floor library Shot Blasting for Concrete Prep Ask when shot blasting belongs in Edmonton concrete prep versus diamond grinding so commercial or garage coatings get the profile the data sheet requires. Updated September 8, 2026 Ask Denis about a flake floor Shot blasting is a mechanical preparation method. A machine propels steel media at concrete, then recovers media and debris through an integrated process. On the right open floor, it can produce a consistent prepared path. It is not a universal answer for oil contamination, weak concrete, edges, stairs, tight rooms, every old coating, or every specified surface profile. For local scope options, see our Surface Preparation. The useful question is not “Do you shot blast?” It is “Why is this method appropriate for these areas and this coating system?” Start with the condition, not the machine Before equipment arrives, map the slab. Record old coatings, adhesive, curing compounds if known, patches, cracks, joints, spalls, drains, trenches, embedded metal, low spots, and possible contamination. Mark fixed equipment and areas where the machine cannot travel. In an Edmonton facility, include wet loading-door zones and places that collect de-icer or oil. Cleaning and contamination removal generally need resolution before blasting. Steel media is not a degreaser.
